close_reason: Re-parented to workspace-wide rustdoc sweep epic JMAP-ibyi per the bead's 'one sweep PR' framing + canonical-template rule.
description:
cargo clippy -p jmap-chat-server --all-features -- -W clippy::pedantic surfaces three doc-comment lint families at high volume:

- 93 doc_markdown / item in documentation is missing backticks — type names, method names, and crate names mentioned in doc-comments without backtick quoting. Example: a doc comment mentioning ChatBackend reads as English text in cargo doc instead of as a linked identifier.
- 49 missing_errors_doc — pub fn returning Result without a "# Errors" section in its rustdoc. Required by clippy's docs guidance and by the workspace's stated intent to publish a kit (downstream consumers reading the rustdoc want to know what each error variant means).
- 11 missing_panics_doc — pub fn that may panic (.unwrap(), .expect(), explicit panic!) without a "# Panics" section. Critical for the kit's public surface because consumers calling into MemoryBackend (the only pub-surface .expect()s in the crate live there) need to know the panic preconditions.

Site distribution (rough, from the clippy output):
- backend.rs, lib.rs: bulk of missing_errors_doc (the handler-registration surface)
- memory.rs: bulk of missing_panics_doc (the .lock().unwrap() and .expect() sites)
- across all .rs files: doc_markdown is uniformly distributed

Three lints; one sweep PR; one bead so the work shows up on a single sprint. The fix is mechanical:
1. Wrap identifiers in backticks in doc comments (sed-able for many sites; some require judgment to distinguish identifier-mentioned-as-identifier from identifier-mentioned-as-English-word).
2. Add "# Errors" sections enumerating the SetError / BackendSetError variants each fn can return.
3. Add "# Panics" sections to MemoryBackend methods that hold std::sync::Mutex (poison-panic if a previous holder panicked) and to the .expect()s tagged 'OS CSPRNG must be available' etc.

Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates": check jmap-mail-server for the same pattern density before sweeping; the rustdoc-quality gap is likely workspace-wide and a one-shot sweep across all 30+ crates is the efficient form. The propagation epic JMAP-76wm (workspace README convention sweep, closed) shows the workspace already accepts this kind of cross-crate doc polish.

What goes wrong if left: this is the kind of pre-publish polish that publishers always wish they did before 1.0. RUSTDOCFLAGS=--cfg docsrs -D warnings cargo +nightly doc (the workspace's documented pre-publish gate per workspace AGENTS.md's RustCrypto Contribution Workflow) does not yet check pedantic doc lints but reviewers do read rustdoc and unbacktick'd identifiers look amateurish in a published API.
title: rustdoc polish sweep: 93 missing-backticks, 49 missing-Errors, 11 missing-Panics under clippy::pedantic
